te THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE M. GANGA RAO CRIMINAL PETITION No.2544 of 2020 ORDER:
This criminal petition, under Sections 437 & 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, is filed by the petitioners - A2 to A5 requesting to grant regular bail in case in Crime No.685 of 2020 on the file of Kanchikacherla Police Station, Krishna District,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 328, 269, 270, 273 read with 34 IPC and Sections 5, 22 of COTP Act and Section 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii) of the Narcotic Drugs And Psychotropic Substances, Act, 1985.

entities.text: Narcotic Drugs And Psychotropic Substances, Act, 1985
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The case of the prosecution is that on 19.06.2020 at about 03.30 PM the police noticed the petitioners loading contraband from Mahindra Truck Auto: into an Auto.

On that the SI of police apprehended the petitioners and on interrogation of the petitioners in the presence of mediators, it is revealed that the petitioners used to purchase Gutkha, Khainees, Cigarettes and Ganja from A1, who is resident of Hyderabad.

Petitioner no.4 brought the contraband from A1 ina Mahindra Truck and while the petitioners were shifting the 'contraband from Mahindra Truck into Auto,
the police apprehended the petitioners.

The SI arrested the petitioners in the presence of mediators under a mediators report and seized prohibited Gutkha,
Khaini packets and cigarette packets from the possession of the petitioners.
5 % kgs of ganja is also seized from the petitioners under cover of mediators report.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that insofar as the offences under COTP Act are concerned, this Court in a series of judgments Oakhwn> held that police have no jurisdiction to register the crime and investigate and if any offence is made out, the Food Safety Officer is alone entitled to investigate the crime in terms of Section 42 of Food Safety and Standards Act.

Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioners are falsely implicated in the case and the alleged seizure of the contraband of 5 % Kgs Ganja is made contrary to the provision of Section 50 of NDPS Act and that merits of the case apart, the quantity of Ganja involved is 5 % Kgs and it is not a commercial quantity and the bar under Section 37 of NDPS Act does not apply to the case on hand and the petitioners are in judicial custody since 19.06.2020.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed for granting bail, inter alia, stating that investigation is pending.
Having regard to the facts and submissions and on perusal of the record, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled for bail.

Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the petitioners are directed to be enlarged on bail on their executing personal bonds for a sum of Rs.25,000/-
